# GEO

*Concept* · also written AEO · generative engine optimisation · generative engine optimization

Generative engine optimisation (and its twin AEO): labels for optimising for AI answers, which Google says good SEO already covers.

**Glossary** (*GEO and AEO*): Labels for generative engine optimisation and answer engine optimisation. Google's answer: don't worry about the name, good SEO is good GEO and AEO.

Narrative: the topic [SEO vs GEO](../topics/seo-vs-geo.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

7 claims mention it: 6 shown or said at the event (1 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs, 4 nothing to verify), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C050`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google's answer to 'SEO is dead, long live GEO' is not to worry about the name: good SEO is good GEO and AEO. `[D1-C050, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C049`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Gary Illyes argued that GEO is a label invented to create a new field and is not needed. Understanding how SEO works is enough. `[D1-C049, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C059`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: The opening keynote closed with the advice to think about UEO, user engine optimisation, next to SEO and GEO: focus on the user and the rest will follow. `[D1-C059, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C296`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker argued for adopting the GEO label as the industry's chance to leave behind the bad reputation SEO built, unlike Google's view earlier the same day that the new name is not needed. `[D1-C296, stage, Thiago Pojda, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C426`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: Asked whether optimising for AI search can hurt classic search or the reverse, a Google panelist said yes, pointing to questionable GEO advice published online that he declined to name. `[D1-C426, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C496`](../sessions/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Nik Vujic said his agency uses the combined data to test whether good SEO is good GEO, and that the answer is 'it depends': for one client it found pages that performed better in generative AI features and LLMs than in standard search. `[D3-C496, stage, Nik Vujic, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C213`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Analysis: Tactics sold as AI visibility or GEO, such as hidden text aimed at AI answers, mass-produced pages for fan-out queries or keyword-stuffed passages, are judged under the same spam policies as classic ranking manipulation. `[D3-C213, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
